task.title: Versioned delta handshake
task.specification: config={version:nonnegative integer,value:integer}. Events delta={type:'delta',base,version,delta}, snapshot={type:'snapshot',version,value}, ack={type:'ack',version}. Keep current version/value, acknowledged=-1 and a snapshot-request latch. A delta with base=current and version>base applies, clears the latch; any other delta with version<=current is ignored; any remaining delta emits {type:'snapshot',base:current} once while latched and leaves state unchanged. A snapshot with version>current replaces version/value and clears the latch; same-version same-value is ignored; same-version different-value requests a snapshot once; older snapshots are ignored. Ack sets acknowledged=current only when its version equals current; older/future acks are ignored. After version advances, previously acknowledged remains as a historical version. Output {version,value,acknowledged,effects}, where effects is the one request object or []. A request is rearmed only by a successfully applied newer delta or snapshot. Return one JSON output per event; state is opaque JSON, initially null. Objects in outputs have exactly the documented keys; map keys are unordered, arrays are ordered. Sorted/lexicographic string order compares Unicode scalar values (code points), with a shorter prefix first. Numeric inputs/values and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers. Integral JSON number notations such as 1 and 1.0 denote the same number, while booleans are distinct. Strings contain Unicode scalar values (no unpaired surrogates). Decoded imported values outside these limits are invalid frames. There are at most 48 events. Unknown/invalid operations have the behavior below. Each instance starts fresh. Hidden ordinary cases vary legal values; boundary cases emphasize equality, empty data and duplicates; adversarial cases reorder and conflict; shift cases use longer traces and more identities within the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Archival provenance and original order
matchedCard.relation: The origin and original arrangement of records preserve relationships that can be lost when the same contents are rearranged arbitrarily. A later description or arrangement is distinct from evidence of the organization in which the records were produced.
assumptions: The origin or original order is known or supported by evidence.
Relationships among records contribute to their interpretation.
matchedCard.boundary: Original order can be lost or disrupted. A newly devised arrangement does not establish that it was the historical arrangement, and provenance does not make every recorded claim true.
matchedCard.source_fact: The National Archives explains provenance, preserving or restoring original order, and devising arrangements when necessary, emphasizing the evidential significance of context.

shuffledCard.label: Seed banking
shuffledCard.relation: Preserving a reserve and preserving its ability to reactivate are different conditions. Suitable material remains in controlled storage, while periodic sample recovery provides evidence of continued viability. Duplicate holdings reduce dependence on one location.
assumptions: The material tolerates the chosen storage treatment.
Samples provide relevant evidence about the collection they represent.
Duplicate collections remain identifiable as corresponding holdings.
shuffledCard.boundary: Some material cannot survive drying or freezing. Successful retention alone does not demonstrate viability, and sampled viability is not certainty about every stored item.
shuffledCard.source_fact: Kew stores suitable dried seeds in cold vaults, periodically tests germination, and commonly duplicates holdings in their country of origin. Some seeds do not tolerate conventional storage.

sources.title: How to preserve seeds for the future

initial.explanation: The conditional rule is: process each event against the current version/value; only strictly newer, causally valid updates advance state, while conflicting or causally invalid updates request one snapshot until a successful advance rearms the latch. Acknowledgements only record the current version.
initial.mapping: config.version/value initialize v/x; acknowledged is a, and the request latch is l. Each event maps to one output snapshot of v, x, a, and effects.
initial.assumptions: Inputs follow the stated legal numeric and JSON constraints. Unknown event types are no-ops because no other behavior is specified.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!applies(input)||!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;let c=input.config,s={v:c.version,x:c.value,a:-1,l:false};for(let i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){let e=input.events[i],f=[],t=e&&e.type;if(t==='delta'){if(e.base===s.v&&e.version>s.v){s.v=e.version;s.x+=e.delta;s.l=false}else if(e.version>s.v&&!s.l){s.l=true;f=[{type:'snapshot',base:s.v}]}}else if(t==='snapshot'){if(e.version>s.v){s.v=e.version;s.x=e.value;s.l=false}else if(e.version===s.v&&e.value!==s.x&&!s.l){s.l=true;f=[{type:'snapshot',base:s.v}]}}else if(t==='ack'&&e.version===s.v)s.a=s.v;let q={version:s.v,value:s.x,acknowledged:s.a,effects:f};if(JSON.stringify(q)!==JSON.stringify(output[i]))return false}return true}

final.explanation: Maintains version, value, historical acknowledgement, and the snapshot-request latch across events. Valid newer deltas require the current base; newer snapshots replace state. Invalid newer deltas and conflicting same-version snapshots request one snapshot until a successful advance rearms the latch. Older or duplicate updates are ignored, and acknowledgements only apply to the current version.
